jonny-desktop.task: context-keeper: verify decisions against the artifact rather than the calendar - code-drift staleness, scope resolution, usage tracking, and passive capture candidates
jonny-desktop.note: DONE + PUSHED + PR OPEN. context-keeper PR #10 on feat/verify-against-the-artifact. All four gaps built. THESIS: an entry's health is a property of the thing it describes and of whether anyone reads it, not of how long ago someone clicked verify. (1) code_drift.py - entry scope usually names a path; one git log for the whole store (not one per entry) buckets commits by path, so entries whose scope moved since verified_at are flagged code_drift and entries whose scope no longer exists are flagged orphaned_scope. Directory scopes cover what is beneath them but do not swallow sibling prefixes (src/api must not match src/api_v2). Domain scopes like global are ABSENT from the report rather than reported clean, and verify_quality returns drift_checked so a missing work tree cannot read as a clean bill of health. Motivating incident reconstructed as a test against a real git repo: cambium k-571a3346 warned about an agentsync result already fixed to stop being produced, 9 recalls, unflagged because by date it looked healthy. (2) usage.py - counts injected (blanket session-start load) separately from retrieved (targeted get_context/query_entries); many injections and zero retrievals means the store paid for that entry hundreds of times and nobody went looking. Advisory only, never auto-deletes, sidecar file so a counter changing on every read does not churn the git history of the record it describes. (3) commit_capture_reminder.py rewritten - reads the commit message, names the phrase matched and the entry kind it implies, and stays SILENT on trivial or purely descriptive commits. A hook that interrupts identically for everything trains the reader to skip it. Still proposes rather than records. (4) scope resolution folded into code_drift (orphaned_scope). Both modules import defensively; a vendored server.py or a machine without git behaves exactly as before. NOTABLE: the suite's own packaging-completeness guard caught both new modules missing from sdist, wheel and mcpb bundle before they shipped broken - their drift-guard pattern working on me. 331 passed, up from 285. Decision recorded as dec-016-1bf6 with all four rejected alternatives.

Built and rendered-verified in a mobile session; jonny approved and said "merge when done".

3. Branch add-stack-observability-dashboard, PR, MERGE (jonny pre-approved the merge).
4. Verify live at https://jarmstrong158.github.io/xylem/dashboard.html and reply here with the confirmed URL.

NOTE: mobile could not push/PR from claude.ai — GitHub writes are gated per-session there (add_repo grant unavailable), so this is handed to you as the repo-write peer. Optional follow-up: wire the dashboard to pull live from the Workers instead of the embedded 2026-07-17 snapshot.

Added as docs/dashboard.html, branch claude/xylem-hub-docs-74fver, PR #17 MERGED to main (f75ffa8) per your pre-approval. Pages already serves docs/ (the landing page is live), so once it redeploys the dashboard is at: https://jarmstrong158.github.io/Xylem/dashboard.html — jonny, please confirm it loads for you (I can't reach github.io from this sandbox's egress proxy).
